/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 141

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture141

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 141](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`,
`tree(G) ≥ ⌊girth(G) / 2⌋ - 1 + max_v l(v)`
where `tree(G)` is the number of vertices of a largest induced tree subgraph,
`girth(G)` is the length of the shortest cycle (0 if acyclic), and
`l(v) = indepNeighbors G v` is the independence number of the neighbourhood of `v`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture141 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    (G.girth / 2 : ℤ) - 1 + ((Finset.univ.sup (indepNeighborsCard G) : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤
    (largestInducedTreeSize G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `largestInducedTreeSize` invariant is a natural number (nonneg). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ largestInducedTreeSize G := Nat.zero_le _

/-- The path graph `P₃` has 3 vertices; `n P₃ = 3`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : Fintype.card (Fin 3) = 3 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture141

findings.description: Line 46 uses `(G.girth / 2 : ℤ)`, which is integer division and therefore floors half the girth. The source uses the unrounded quantity girth(G)/2. Writing L for the maximum neighborhood independence number and T for the largest induced tree size, the source's inequality is equivalent to `ceil(girth/2) - 1 + L ≤ T`, not the formalized `floor(girth/2) - 1 + L ≤ T`. For odd girth 2k+1, Lean gives the lower bound k−1+L instead of k+L, losing one vertex. The hypotheses do not restrict girth to be even. The floor added in the docstring repeats the same error.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaVina's Written on the Wall II, conjecture 141 (July 19, 2005), states: “If G is a simple connected graph, then tree(G) ≥ (1/2)*girth - 1 + maximum of λ(v).” There is no floor. This appears identically in all.html and open.html; see https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html . The linked definitions identify tree(G) and λ(v) as vertex cardinalities.
findings.suggested_fix: Use genuine division, for example `((G.girth : ℝ) / 2) - 1 + ((Finset.univ.sup (indepNeighborsCard G) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (largestInducedTreeSize G : ℝ)`. Alternatively, keep the integer inequality and replace `(G.girth / 2 : ℤ)` with `⌈(G.girth : ℝ) / 2⌉`. Update the docstring to state the unrounded source bound, or its equivalent ceiling form.

review.notes: The live site was unreachable, so the comparison uses archived copies, including the July 2026 conjecture lists. Both lists mark 141 open, agreeing with the file. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors and prove the floor interpretation, the source inequality's equivalence to the ceiling bound, and the one-vertex arithmetic gap at odd girth. I also checked the supporting definitions, finite-supremum boundedness, empty and singleton inputs, K₂, K₃, paths, and small cycles. The zero-girth convention causes no additional boundary defect: the corrected bound was proved for every connected acyclic graph. Both sanity-check declarations are mathematically correct.

not_demonstrated.reason: The rounding discrepancy weakens the lower bound but does not give a counterexample or a trivial proof of the full graph inequality. The existing floor/ceiling calculations use arbitrary numerical values, not verified graph invariants, so they do not qualify as a demonstration of this declaration. A proof of the full statement would require substantive graph-theoretic arguments.

submission.summary: No qualifying trivial demonstration was found. No trivial_proof.lean file was created.
submission.gave_up_reason: I cannot honestly prove or refute the declaration as stated in a handful of Lean lines. An isolated arithmetic rounding example would demonstrate only the numerical discrepancy, not settle the actual graph statement.

submission.summary: Changed the inequality to use real division, preserving the source's unrounded girth/2 bound, and removed the floor from the docstring. No other declarations were changed. The edited file compiles with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
